The matrix (Step C) refuses to run unless this file is committed, all four answers are non-empty, noiseBand equals pilot.json's calibrated band, and the digest matches the working tree.

stepCAmendment: §8 amendment, 2026-07-29 (Step C, pre-matrix — no timed matrix data existed, so nothing is invalidated; the pilot and its band stand unchanged). The frozen surface gains: (1) closures for the seven Step-C residuals the previous adversarialReviewRecord enumerates — attempt-keyed washout markers (attemptId/forAttemptId), a persisted washout horizon (washoutUntilEpochMs), typed control-plane invalidation (ControlPlaneFailure → outcome invalidated-control-plane: replay in slot, never charged to the R1/R2 allowance, durably capped per pos at 3 attempts — a deliberate, reviewed extension beside the frozen R1–R6 taxonomy), the C6 typed replay ledger (one objective-external rerun per fixture×driver; mismatches and content-failures permanent; outcome vocabulary match/mismatch/content-failure/attempt-error mapping to G1 vs G2), R5-record aggregate preservation, env-manifest dedup by hash sequenced after identity acceptance, and per-unit straddle COUNTS with resume refusal at ≥2; (2) the four Step-C executors (benchScore/benchReport pure readers; benchBoundary, benchConcurrencyProbe, benchOption3 evidence generators) — each frozen and adversarially reviewed BEFORE collecting data, per the Step-B freeze-scoping amendment; (3) evidence-integrity hardening: every runs.jsonl row stamps its frozenSurfaceDigest and both resume and scoring refuse foreign-freeze/foreign-identity rows; scoring/report read the logs and probe artifacts as COMMITTED HEAD blobs and load all frozen inputs from the rows' own harness commit; append-only is enforced by committed-prefix byte identity with crash-tail repair (seal complete JSON, truncate torn bytes, never inside the committed prefix); pinning-family commands refuse to run post-ratification; (4) RunRecord schema additions (attemptId, washoutUntilEpochMs, requestClassSuccesses — semantic per-class successes feeding R2, straddledReset/controlPlaneFailed fact fields counted independently of outcome precedence, g2PositiveFailures scored across all attempts, frozenSurfaceDigest, attempts.noResponse); (5) digest inputs now include pilot.json and acquisition-diagnostics.json. R4 outcome precedence: re-pin > drift-restart > straddle > control-plane > unit-failure, with straddle/control-plane FACTS recorded on every row regardless of the winning outcome.
environmentAmendment: §8 environment amendment, 2026-07-29 (pre-evidence — the first matrix attempt under the original identity was aborted with zero usable terminal rows and is preserved verbatim in runs-aborted-2026-07-29-env1.jsonl; per §8 an environment change restarts the whole matrix on a fresh log). CAUSE, measured: a persistent foreign GraphQL consumer (~4 points/min) on the operator identity sondrateconsulting-ryan — surviving the quiescing of VS Code, its GitHub extensions, and every local gh process (0.25 s process sampling found only the bench's own spawns; consumption continued through hands-off observation windows; the residual suspect is the desktop agent app's own GitHub integration, which cannot be disabled from inside the session it hosts). Under the frozen §4.5 rules that traffic R3-invalidates nearly every row (one position burned five attempts) and, by pinning the graphql reset epoch, produced an R4 straddle with a second-strike halt exposure. RESOLUTION, per §4.8's own sanctioned alternative ('use a dedicated account and re-record the login fingerprint') and chosen by the decision-maker (rvo, recorded in-session 2026-07-29): all timed matrix data runs under the dedicated bot account `rvobot` (quiescence verified: buckets flat over observation), scoped to the bench processes alone via GH_TOKEN passthrough (both sanitized spawn envs allowlist it; the operator's ambient gh identity and every non-bench consumer stay on the original account). Machine, network, toolchain, and every pinned artifact are unchanged; the harness surface digest is unchanged (672ec6bc…). The ratified 1.25 noise band STANDS: the §4.7 formula's floor bound the pilot spread (1.034) with a 0.216 margin, the pilot's role is band calibration (declared non-decision) rather than cross-environment timing comparison, and the walls feeding it were measured on this same machine and network. Two measured observations are carried to the report: (1) REST content/tree reads on the original identity billed to NO rate_limit resource (core unchanged across hundreds of 200s, pilot history identical) — scoring is invariant to this via §4.6's larger-governs pairing; (2) the aborted attempt's sidecar demonstrates the R3/R4 machinery detecting real foreign interference live. AMENDMENT-REVIEW REMEDIATION (round 1 → REQUEST-CHANGES with two findings, both closed pre-evidence): (1) the declared bench identity is now FAIL-CLOSED — makeEngine refuses to proceed when BENCH_EXPECTED_LOGIN is set and /user resolves to any other login, so a missing or mistyped GH_TOKEN can never silently collect data under the operator's stored auth (this is a frozen-surface change; the digest below is re-recorded accordingly); (2) PRECISION on the one-credential claim: git-protocol transport to the public corpus is ANONYMOUS, in the bench exactly as in production — git consults the pinned credential helper only on an authentication challenge, and public repositories never challenge. Forcing proactive git auth would alter the very transport semantics under measurement (the pilot, the acquisition diagnostics, and the M-series all ran helper-on-challenge). The credential binding therefore governs the API planes (REST/GraphQL — the identity-scoped, rate-limited, R3-reconciled resources), while git-plane traffic remains bound by the manifest's machine and network. Stated here so the report can say it plainly. ROUND-2 CLOSURE: the identity binding moved into THIS tracked record — benchLogin above is enforced by every engine construction once ratification.json exists, independent of any launcher or environment variable (round 2's residual: an untracked launcher was the only thing setting the expectation).
